digest.component_or_area: overlap judge — Stage-2 ticket-pair verdict engine
propositions: Stage-2 overlap judge re-sends the query ticket digest verbatim in the user message on every call within a batch (12 of 12 measured), despite it being identical across all calls and therefore uncacheable in the volatile user block

The query digest is hoisted from per-call user instructions into the system prompt so it sits inside the cacheable prefix, requiring one keyword-only argument on judge_one to specify which side is hoisted and substituting a fixed reference string into the vacated slot

The measured system prefix of 846 tokens (base 423 + digest 241–362) falls below the measured 1024-token cache floor for claude-sonnet-4-6, yielding zero cache hits and a measured +936 token (+5.8%) regression despite correct implementation

Precision is preserved on all 12 ordered pairs: relations, shared artifacts, and surface findings identical between baseline and hoisted builds, confirming the pointer-for-inline-digest substitution does not degrade judgment accuracy

The sequential judge loop (no parallelization) ensures the first call warms the prefix and remaining N-1 calls read it; parallelization is explicitly withheld because fanning out cold calls would turn 1 cache write into N premium writes (a regression), requiring a warm-up-first sequencing requirement if parallelism is added later
